subject: Brightwell private cluster: deployment handoff & ops checklist

Subject: Private cluster deployment — preflight & handoff

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We finished internal sign-off on the compliance side and we
are ready to start the on-prem deployment planning. Before we schedule the technical handoff,
we wanted to confirm a few high-level items so our ops and procurement teams are aligned: 

- Target cluster footprint: 8 application nodes (general compute) + 2 inference GPU nodes (A100 equivalent) + 3 infra nodes (control-plane/monitoring).
- Preferred storage: NVMe local for inference caches, shared block for long-term model artifacts (we currently run an on-prem Ceph cluster but can stand up a dedicated PVC backend).
- Network: private VLANs per tenant; firewall rules managed by our network team.
- SOC2 evidence: they will need a list of what logs are collected and whether KV cache persists on disk.

Can you confirm Redwood’s recommended node pool split and the preflight checklist you typically use for these on-prem installs? Also, we can host a 60-minute handoff on Wednesday 3/2 or Friday 3/4 — what works for your team?

Thanks,
Annika
Ops Lead — Brightwell Health

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Private cluster deployment — preflight & handoff

Annika — thanks for the clear summary. Below are the answers and a short preflight I attached as PDF (brightwell_preflight_checklist.pdf).

Quick confirmations and recommendations: 
- Node pools: we recommend 3 logical pools: control/infra (3 nodes, small CPU/memory, pinned etcd + control-plane), general compute (8 nodes, 32vCPU/128GB typical), and inference (2 nodes with GPUs + local NVMe for model KV cache). Keep inference nodes isolated via nodeSelector and taints.
- Storage: NVMe local as a fast ephemeral cache (CSI local-volume) for token/KV caches; persistent model artifacts should be on a blockstore backed by your Ceph or dedicated SAN exposed via CSI (ReadWriteMany not required for model artifacts if you replicate externally).
- CSI and snapshots: you must run a CSI driver compatible with your block backend — Marissa, I’ve copied a short compatibility note below. Snapshots for backups are recommended nightly for model artifacts.
- Networking: separate VLANs and a dedicated egress path for telemetry. We recommend restricting egress from inference nodes except to Redwood endpoints (if using the private control plane).
- Logs & evidence: Redwood’s agent can ship token-level request logs (anonymized) and host-level metrics. KV cache is ephemeral by default and lives in RAM + local NVMe; we can switch to encrypted local persistence if you need disked evidence for incident reconstruction.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Friday 3/3 10:00–11:00 PT: Technical handoff (Marissa to run infra topics; I’ll cover preflight).
2) Brightwell to share network topology diagram & Ceph admin contact (Annika).
3) Redwood to provide nodepool sizing workbook and a short CSI compatibility checklist (attached nodepool_sizing_v1.xlsx + marissa_cookbook-csi-nvme.txt).
4) Procurement: Karthik, I’ll loop in Laura for contract boundaries and SLAs once the handoff confirms scope.

I’ve attached a one-page preflight checklist and a nodepool sizing workbook. If Friday morning works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

—
Irene Choi
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Annika/Irene — quick technical addendum ahead of the handoff:

Short recommendations (specifics you can use during procurement):
- Inference nodes: 2 x A100-similar GPUs, 1TB NVMe each, 768GB RAM, 48 vCPU. Reserve 20% headroom for burst. Use local NVMe as a write-through cache for the KV store; avoid relying on networked PV for per-token cache.
- General compute: 8 nodes, 32vCPU/128GB/2 x 1TB SSD (or equivalent). Use storageClass fast-block for model downloads and networked backup to Ceph.
- Control plane/infra: 3 nodes (control-plane+etcd if you want HA), 16vCPU/64GB each. Prefer anti-affinity across racks.
- PV strategy: CSI-local for ephemeral caches, RBD/CSI for Ceph-backed block PVs for model artifacts and logs. Consider using an S3-compatible gateway for cold model artifact storage.
- QoS & eviction: mark inference pods as Guaranteed where possible to reduce eviction during pressure. Keep kube-system and monitoring in the infra pool.

Compatibility/limitations:
- If you plan to use older Ceph releases, the snapshot API may be limited; we can provide a small helper daemon to coordinate snapshots if needed.
- For encryption-at-rest on NVMe: depends on drive firmware and procurement choices; we can run dm-crypt wrapper for CSI-local but testing required.

Attached is a short text cookbook of CSI/driver recommendations (marissa_cookbook-csi-nvme.txt) and the Excel workbook Irene attached. During the handoff we’ll walk through the workbook and finalize exact VM sizes.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
